subject: Dedicated capacity discovery — proposed scope & asks
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Walsh <emma@falconpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery — proposed scope & asks

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the detailed runthrough of the FalconPay fraud-detection pipeline. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the success criteria you shared, and the initial scope we recommend for a Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) evaluation.

Quick recap of pain points you raised:
- Unpredictable inference latency during peak settlement windows (spikes to 400–600ms p50 token latency right now).
- High per-token cost from bursty public endpoints; cost jumps during monthly reconciliation runs.
- Need for data isolation and stricter network controls for payment data (PCI-adjacent) — legal prefers dedicated tenancy.
- Requirement for consistent throughput during nightly batch reconciliation (sustained TPS target).

Current stack and constraints you described:
- Inference currently runs on a managed hosted endpoint (multi-tenant) from Vendor X. Model: FalconBERT-XL (decoder-only fine-tuned for reranking).
- Typical payload: 256 token sequences, average batch size today ~1–4, spikes to 32 during reconciles.
- Observability: metrics pushed to internal Grafana; no token-level cost breakdown today.

Success criteria (as discussed) — FalconPay would call a Dedicated eval successful if all of the following are met:
1) Sustained throughput: support 50 TPS sustained for 12+ hour reconciliation window with p95 tail under 250ms.
2) Predictable unit cost: estimated 35–45% lower per-token cost vs current hosted plan at production throughput.
3) Isolation & controls: VPC peering, customer-managed keys for model artifacts, and audit logs retained for 12 months.
4) Operational fit: seamless autoscaling/burst policy to handle 3x short bursts without degraded latency or failed requests.

Initial technical fit / recommended reserved pool for the eval
- Proposed reserved pool: 8 x A100-80GB equivalent capacity (we can map to available instance SKUs in your preferred cloud region).
- Default runtime config: sequence-optimized kernel selection with 8-token KV-cache warmup, continuous batching window 20–30ms for tail latency control.
- Autoscale policy (proposal): maintain 50 TPS baseline, allow automated burst to 150 TPS for up to 15 mins, with a conservative cooldown.
- KV prefix caching: recommend caching hot prefixes (top 5–10) to reduce per-token work during reconciliation.

Asks / follow-ups from Redwood to scope the trial (items we need from FalconPay):
- Representative workload traces for two typical windows: (a) daily traffic, (b) monthly reconciliation spike — ideally 24h of request samples with timestamps and token counts (we will treat these as sensitive).
- A short list of 5 prompts/queries used in reranking so we can validate output quality and latency.
- Network contact for VPC peering and a point of contact in procurement for a short SOW and MSA.

Deliverables we will provide before the pilot start
- A tailored capacity plan mapping to cloud SKU options and cost estimates (attached: throughput-estimates.csv).
- A short playbook for the pilot run (attached: falconpay-dedicated-scope-20260822.pdf) that includes rollback criteria and success measurement.
- A one-week schedule proposal for the eval with checkpoints (technical onboarding, run, review).

Proposed next steps
1) You share workload traces & prompts (ideally by Tue 8/25).
2) Redwood sends formal SOW + reserved-pool sizing by Thu 8/27.
3) Kickoff technical onboarding week of 8/31 (if procurement aligns).

If this matches your understanding, I’ll loop in our cloud team to start sizing SKUs and draft the SOW.

Thanks —

--
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0112

Attachments: falconpay-dedicated-scope-20260822.pdf (summary + runbook), throughput-estimates.csv (prelim numbers)
From: Emma Walsh <emma@falconpay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@falconpay.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery — proposed scope & asks

Thanks Aditya — this is great and aligns with our notes. A couple of clarifications and asks from our side: 

1) The reconciliation window where we saw the worst spikes is 01:00–04:00 UTC on the 1st of each month; sustained 45–60 TPS observed in the last run. If you can size for 50 TPS sustained with 3x burst, that would be perfect.
2) For isolation: Legal will require an inventory of which artifacts live on the dedicated pool (model weights, KV cache). Can you confirm whether Redwood supports HSM-backed keys for model artifact encryption?
3) Procurement would like a draft SOW with pricing bands (baseline reserved vs burst usage) and an estimated timeline to production if the pilot succeeds.

We will send anonymized request samples by Monday (8/24) EOD. Procurement copied here — they’ll coordinate the SOW review.

One more ask: can you include a short note on how rollback/fallback would behave in case of degraded quality during the pilot? We prefer an automatic fallback to a smaller hosted variant rather than fail open.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Emma

--
Emma Walsh
Head of ML Engineering | FalconPay
emma@falconpay.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Walsh <emma@falconpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@falconpay.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 17:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery — proposed scope & asks

Emma — thanks for the quick confirmation and the specifics. Short answers to your clarifying questions below, plus immediate next steps.

- HSM / key management: Yes. Redwood Private/Dedicated supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for model artifacts and blob storage. I’ll include the KMS integration note in the SOW.
- Rollback/fallback behavior: we can configure a policy-based fallback that routes requests to a verified hosted variant when quality or latency thresholds are breached. We’ll provide a canary/health-checking setup and an automatic fallback window (configurable) to avoid fail-open.
- Procurement asks: we will include pricing bands (reserved baseline + metered burst) in the draft SOW. Estimated timeline subject to procurement sign-off: pilot onboarding (1 week), 2-week run, 1-week evaluation and decision — roughly 4 weeks from SOW signature.

Immediate next actions (I’ll own):
1) Redwood cloud team will review the workload traces when you send them on Mon 8/24 and respond with a recommended SKU mapping by Wed 8/26.
2) I’ll circulate a draft SOW and sizing worksheet to procurement by Thu 8/27.
3) Tentatively schedule a 30-minute technical kickoff for Tue 8/31 10:00–10:30 PT (please confirm availability).

If procurement prefers a different cadence for the SOW review, let us know and we’ll adapt. Monica (cc’d) will lead the onboarding plan on our side; Ben will own billing/contract items.

Thanks — looking forward to running the eval.

--
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
